S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic primary psychotic disorder characterized by a combination of positive symptoms (such as delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized thinking/behavior) and negative symptoms (such as diminished motivation, reduced emotional expression, and social withdrawal), with a duration of at least six months and clear functional decline. Onset typically occurs in late adolescence to mid-adulthood, often following a prodromal phase of subtle social and occupational changes. The course is usually relapsing and remitting or chronic, with variable degrees of residual impairment, particularly in negative and cognitive domains. It is distinguished from mood disorders with psychotic features by the presence of psychosis outside of mood episodes, and from brief psychotic or schizophreniform disorders by its longer duration and more pervasive impact on functioning.

patient.personality: She is a calm, methodical cleaner who enjoys gardening, cooking, and making handmade gifts, and tends to take a relaxed, flexible approach to schedules and obligations.
patient.stressor: Carlina’s problems started after she developed a prolonged period of fatigue and vague physical complaints following a winter respiratory illness, which led to several missed shifts and worries about job security at the logistics company where she cleaned vehicles and equipment. Already somewhat forgetful, she became increasingly concerned about her concentration and energy, and began spending more time at home listening to true‑crime podcasts and scrolling health forums, trying to make sense of what she was feeling. Over the following eight months, her husband and coworkers noticed a marked change: she grew quieter, less engaged in her beloved gardening and animal‑shelter volunteering, and more inwardly focused on trying to understand perceived patterns and meanings behind her health issues and events at work, while her work quality and reliability declined. After she was written up for repeated absences and her husband realized she was no longer managing basic household routines or participating in community gatherings, he brought her to a psychiatric clinic out of concern that something more serious than stress or physical illness was going on.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve gotten caught up in certain ideas about what’s happening to me, and I just can’t seem to shake them no matter what people say.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Ever since I got sick in the winter, I’ve been convinced that the people at work and even the folks on those health forums are secretly tracking my symptoms and my missed shifts, like they’re running some kind of experiment on me, and no matter how much my husband tells me that’s impossible, I can’t shake the feeling that the podcasts I listen to and little things my coworkers say are actually coded messages about what they’re doing to my body and my job.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: My husband and coworkers say I’ll just stop in the middle of wiping down a bus or stand frozen in the kitchen with a sponge in my hand for ten or fifteen minutes, staring at one spot or holding my arms in a strange way, and I barely notice them talking to me until they shake my shoulder or raise their voice.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Most days now I just sit on the couch in my sweats, scrolling on my phone or staring at the wall, ignoring texts and calls, with no energy or interest to go out to the garden, cook something nice, visit the animal shelter, or even chat with my husband, and when he tries to cheer me up I feel flat inside and can only manage short, dull answers.
